title: vram-churn-repro-logbook
content:
Purpose: scratch log for a flaky VRAM churn / intermittent OOM seen on rtx-a100 hosts after a model swap. Keep commands, raw errors, quick hypotheses, and a minimal repro recipe.

Context: producing a small inference load against model corpus v3 (gptx-7b-quant) on dedicated pool; intermittent OOMs start ~30m after rollout of a new runtime-host image. Not consistent across hosts, more frequent on nodes that had long uptimes.

Quick environment snapshot:
- host: rdx-infer-a100-08 (nvidia-smi says 40GB A100S)
- kernel: 6.1.52
- driver: 535.113.01
- CUDA toolkit on PATH: /opt/cuda/12.2
- LD_LIBRARY_PATH: /opt/cuda/12.2/lib64:/opt/nvidia/lib64
- container runtime: containerd 1.8, nvidia-container-toolkit v1.13.0
- serving runtime: redwood-runtime commit b3f2d4 (runtime image tag: r-runtime:2026-03-09)
- model: gptx-7b-quant (ggml -> triton wrapper)

First observed: 2026-03-10 15:14 UTC during a canary rollout.

Symptoms observed (raw snippets):
- "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.25 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 37.80 GiB already allocated)"
- kernel log snippet: "NVRM: GPU 0000:1a:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus." (rare, maybe unrelated)
- driver complaint in runtime logs: "failed to initialize nvml: NVML_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED"
- dlopen error (from python): "OSError: /opt/nvidia/lib64/libnvidia-ml.so.1: undefined symbol: nvmlDeviceGetEncoderStats"
- occasional shared object initialization error: "cudaErrorSharedObjectInitFailed: driver library version mismatch"

Commands & probes tried (with quick results):
- nvidia-smi -q -x > /tmp/nvidia-smi-2026-03-10.xml  (no obvious memory leak info; some processes show orphaned cuda contexts)
- ps aux | grep python  -> found runtime worker pids 32114, 32157 (zombies when failing)
- docker exec -it <cid> bash; ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda* -> container sees vendor-provided libcuda symlinked to /usr/lib/libcuda.so.1
- ldd /opt/cuda/12.2/lib64/libcudart.so -> shows it links to /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (OK but check versions)
- strings /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 | grep "Build" -> prints driver build id 535.113.01 (expected)
- export LD_PRELOAD=/opt/nvidia/lib64/libnvidia-ml.so.1; rerun small job -> got immediate dlopen symbol error (nvmlDeviceGetEncoderStats)

Reproducer (minimal, flaky):
1) start a two-worker workload against gptx-7b-quant with sequence length 2048 and batch size 2.
2) after ~20-40 minutes, induce a model variant swap (hot reload) via control plane (POST /v1/models/swap).
3) within 5-25 minutes, one of the worker processes reports OOM and exits; other worker appears to hold many pinned allocations but shows "cudaMalloc returned unknown error" on subsequent attempts.

Notes on patterns:
- nodes with longer uptime (>14d) more likely to hit the problem.
- restarting the runtime process often clears the issue for a while. Full host reboot less frequent in our playbook but seems to be more robust fix.
- affected hosts sometimes show mismatched versions when inspecting container vs host libraries (host has 535 drivers; container imagess sometimes ship cuda 12.1 libs built against prior drivers).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) library shadowing / partial symbol mismatch: some components (triton, nvml, driver shim) link different symbol sets. Hot-reload triggers a dlopen of a module that expects a newer NVML symbol table — leads to subtle NVML init failure and later memory accounting confusion.
2) stale CUDA contexts / fragmentation: repeated model load/unload cycles leave behind orphaned contexts not freed by our runtime; combined with continuous batching results in fragmentation that eventually prevents contiguous allocation requests.
3) driver-side reference leak across dlopen/dlclose boundaries: driver modules not fully tearing down state when a plugin is unloaded — on long-uptime hosts these leaked refs accumulate.
4) kernel/firmware quirk: "GPU has fallen off the bus" implies occasional hardware / PCIe reset; likely separate but may correlate when driver stack is stressed.

Mitigations tried (workable ones):
- immediate: restart runtime worker process (fast) -> recovers in ~30s.
- moderate: force full model preloading on cold start to avoid hot dlopen during traffic (reduces frequency).
- heavier: node reboot -> clears for long period.
- experimental: set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to a single device per worker to limit cross-device shared state -> mixed results.

What I haven't tried yet (next probes):
- run a stripped reproducer outside of container (host binary built with our serving runtime) to see if container boundaries change behaviour.
- instrument NVML calls around model swap to detect nvml init/fail patterns (wrap dlopen and nvmlDeviceGetHandle calls).
- bisect runtime commit that introduced a different plugin loader change (range: 2026-02-20 .. 2026-03-09).
- try building runtime image with static-linked NVML (if possible) to avoid symbol resolution with host libs.
- run valgrind-like leak detection across repeated dlopen cycles (heavy, but would catch leaks).

Playbook notes for on-call (short):
- if OOMs start: first, restart worker process; if recovery not stable within 3 restarts, escalate and plan host reboot.
- capture /var/log/messages and dmesg, nvml logs, and runtime core dumps.
- add temp debug env: RUNTIME_DEBUG_NVML=1 to collect more NVML trace.

Relevant links / tickets / slack threads:
- jira: INF-3421 (canary rollout incident)
- slack thread: #infra-runtime -> thread ts: 1678453200.000200 (reference in logs)
- github PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/812 (plugin loader tweaks)

Raw errors pasted below for searchability:
"RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.25 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 37.80 GiB already allocated)\n  File \"/app/runtime/worker.py\", line 412, in handle_request\n    out = model.generate(...)\ncudaError(3): initialization error\n"
"OSError: /opt/nvidia/lib64/libnvidia-ml.so.1: undefined symbol: nvmlDeviceGetEncoderStats"
"NVML_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED"
"cudaErrorSharedObjectInitFailed: driver library version mismatch"

Notes to self: use distinct naming for temporary reproducer images; keep track of host uptime correlation; add a small periodic cleanup worker that calls nvmlDeviceReset? (dangerous)

Next actions:
- 2026-03-13: kick off a runtime bisect (assign: @alice-rodriguez)
- 2026-03-14: run host-level reproducer outside of container (assign: me)
- instrument NVML in debug build (assign: @samuel-chen)

Status: draft and exploratory. Save copies of logs to /tmp/vram-churn-logs/<host>-YYYYMMDD
